extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors preparing synopses for agent/editor submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting concise synopses (1-, 3-, and 5-page) to include with agent/editor submissions that clearly convey plot, character arcs, and ending while preserving authorial voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare multiple length versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a one-page, three-page, and five-page synopsis ready (three- and five-page versions double-spaced) so you don’t have to scramble when an agent requests a specific length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explicitly recommends keeping multiple versions on hand because different agents ask for different lengths; prepare one-page plus longer double-spaced versions to meet requests quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start at the Beginning and Go to the End
rubrics_metrics.description: Your synopsis should cover your story from start to finish, outlining major plot points without leaving the reader in suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spoilers are not just okay but essential — reveal twists and the ending so the agent/editor can understand the complete story arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Major Spoilers and the Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t shy away from revealing twists or the conclusion; the synopsis must show how the story resolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing the ending helps agents/editors assess the plot’s viability and whether you can 'stick the landing.' This is repeatedly emphasized as a necessary element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Excessive Backstory
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the main plot and character development rather than long background material that can bog down pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much backstory detracts from the synopsis’s pacing and clarity; include only what’s necessary to understand the plot and characters’ drives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Clarity and Conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be straightforward — a synopsis is not the place to showcase every creative element of your prose or to use query-style hooks or tricks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep language direct and concise. Avoid literary devices or a ‘hooky’ query approach; clarity about plot and stakes is the priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Your Voice (in a restrained way)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the synopsis should be less dramatic than the narrative, it should still reflect the unique voice of your writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strike a balance: let some authorial voice show to convey tone, but restrain dramatics so the plot remains clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Story Structure and Hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the synopsis to showcase your story’s structure and the element(s) that make it hook-worthy to agents or editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The synopsis serves as a tool to demonstrate the plot makes sense and to highlight what makes the book compelling; agents use it to decide whether to invest further time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Multiple POVs and Timelines for Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: For stories with multiple points of view or non-linear timelines, prioritize clarity by segmenting each character’s arc or following the clearest timeline for plot unfolding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Megan suggests either laying out each POV character’s arc separately or arranging events in the timeline that best serves the plot’s clear presentation; the goal is to avoid confusing the reader of the synopsis.
